turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hang on, this thing logged me out again. Okay, I'm back. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I went to my cousin's wedding and ever since I've been throwing up and having diarrhea. Sorry, it's kind of gross.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Gross is fine, I hear worse before lunch. When was the wedding?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturday, up in Dayton. Rehearsal dinner was Friday night. The sick part... I don't know, doctor. Sunday morning? Or late Saturday. I can't pin it down.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Screen just jumped. Say that start time one more time?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday morning I woke up and vomited. Diarrhea hit Sunday afternoon. And it's still both, kind of.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Today's Wednesday, so that's about three days.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The throwing up and the diarrhea feel longer though. Four days, maybe five. I don't know.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many times are you going to the bathroom?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I gave up counting. Eight, ten? Since breakfast, maybe six. It's all a blur.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): And it's watery?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, watery. Kind of yellow. Sorry.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood in it, or anything black?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. I actually looked, my mom made me.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the vomit?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Food at first, then just this yellow liquid.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still vomiting today, or has that eased?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I retched once this morning but I don't think anything came up.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever or chills with it?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose I felt warm Sunday night. I never took my temperature. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): What did you eat there? Buffet, seafood, stuff sitting out?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): The buffet, yeah. Shrimp, chicken in a cream sauce, cake. I don't know which one got me.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else from the wedding sick?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): My cousin texted me. Her husband and two bridesmaids have the same thing. So it's not just me.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any trips outside the country recently?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just Dayton. We drove up and back.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hold on, the med list is blank and this cursor's stuck. What have you been taking?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Imodium. The pharmacist said if it might be from the food I should skip it, but I took it anyway so I could survive the car ride home.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Loperamide. Dose? The box wiped on my screen, say it again.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I think it's two milligrams? Maybe. I don't know, doctor, I left the box at home. I take two capsules to start, then another one whenever I go.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): And you're doing that every loose stool, the way the label says?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. Sometimes I forget, sometimes I take an extra. I don't know.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else in the mix? Pepto, an antibiotic, a prescription?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I chewed a couple Pepto tablets yesterday morning, then I stopped. Didn't do a thing. No antibiotics.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any medicines?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ongoing problems? Diabetes, thyroid, any bowel disease?

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I'm healthy. Well, actually, at my physical last year they ran a blood sugar and they said it was borderline. I don't know the number. I never went back. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline, no number, and nobody started you on a medicine.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. No medicine. I can't even remember if I was fasting.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not chasing that today. Come on up on the table, let me look.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mouth is dry. Lips are a little cracked. That's mild dehydration.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been so thirsty. And I don't think I've peed since last night. Or maybe once. I don't know.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is a hundred and twelve. Blood pressure is one hundred and two over sixty-eight. Temp's thirty-seven point three, this machine's stuck on Celsius, ignore that.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Belly's soft. Some tenderness low down, no guarding. You're not flinching me off.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): It cramps in waves, though. Mostly right before I have to run to the bathroom.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain anyplace else? Chest, burning when you pee, headache?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just the stomach cramps and the bathroom part. Head's fine.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, thinking out loud, ignore the typing. Same meal, a few other guests down with it, watery diarrhea and vomiting a few days. Could be a virus that went through the wedding, could be bacteria off the shrimp or that cream sauce. I am not going to stamp this food poisoning, and I am not starting an antibiotic on a hunch.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I need a stool test, or no?
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. If you're not better in a couple of days, or if you see blood, then we send a stool sample. I'm not ordering it sitting here.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): And the Imodium, do I keep going with it?
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd rather you stop. If this is infectious, loperamide just parks the germ in there. Stop it.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Even with the car and work and all that? I don't know, doctor, it was miserable without it.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): I get it. Stop it anyway. What actually helps is fluid. Small sips of an oral rehydration drink, Pedialyte or the drugstore version, through the day. Big gulps and you'll just throw them back up.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Is plain water okay? Or Gatorade, that's what I've got at home.

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Water's fine next to it. Gatorade works if that's what's in the fridge, the rehydration stuff is better. If you can't keep even sips down, you come back the same day, that can turn into needing IV fluid.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): One sec, I'm trying to get this note to save. There it goes.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): No rush. Side note, my cousin's dog ate cake off the floor and puked on the dance floor during the dollar dance. Whole scene. Not why I'm here, obviously.

[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha. Okay. If you are not keeping fluids down, or you get dizzy, or there's blood, come back sooner. Otherwise, if you are not clearly better in forty-eight hours, I want you back in this office.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Forty-eight hours. What if I'm like half better?
[SEG0062] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still come. If you are not clearly better in forty-eight hours, half-better counts. I want to see you.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I eat anything? I'm kind of afraid to.
[SEG0064] person_1 (DOCTOR): Once the vomiting eases off, bland food, crackers, rice, bananas. Don't force a real dinner tonight.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): I had two glasses of wine at the reception. I don't drink much otherwise. I don't know if that messed me up.

[SEG0066] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two glasses didn't do this. Skip alcohol till you're well, it just irritates the gut. We're done, unless the computer eats the note. Stop the loperamide, keep sipping, and if you are not clearly better in forty-eight hours, you're back.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
